body:
Engram needs a reusable, versioned agreement between ontology packs and the engine so a new compatible pack can produce its declared artifacts, evidence and retrieval behavior without pack-specific engine code. Loading YAML or accepting an event does not currently establish that agreement.

This is an umbrella **feature/enhancement**, not a replacement for existing defect issues. PDLC is the full-pack acceptance case; CRM and an unfamiliar fixture pack establish generality. Astra medium review verdict: **ready with conditions**. Blocking decisions must be resolved before their affected implementation slices; no compatibility sign-off is implied.

### Deliverables
- Explicit pack capability/activation checks, owned event contracts and authorized cross-pack subscribers.
- Reviewed source-to-event mappings and shared validation/trust across single, batch, import and webhook ingress.
- Defined event-to-artifact semantics: missing versus null, bounded list expansion, conditional/no-op behavior, ordering/stale-write policy and property ownership.
- Immutable duplicate policy for same ID/different content, including source-binding revision changes.
- API/worker interpretation compatibility and available historical rules before accepting new metadata; safe replay/upgrade policy.
- Exact relationship/transition evidence and correlated applied/skipped/deferred/failed/unknown processing outcomes, reusing current surfaces where possible.
- Reusable pack conformance fixtures with expected normalized events, exact graph deltas, forbidden effects and retrieval answers/evidence.

### Implementation sequence and review findings
| Slice | Required design/acceptance work | Existing issues |
|---|---|---|
|1: contracts and fixtures|PE-01 missing/null/cardinality; PE-02 ordering/property ownership; PE-04 duplicates; PE-05 revision/obligations; PE-06 capabilities; PE-08 exact fixtures for all23 PDLC events plus third pack|#4 #5 #8 #9 #17 #22 #28 #29|
|2: shared ingress|All-route validation/trust; persisted metadata round trip and compatible/refused N/N-1 worker behavior; valid/invalid unfamiliar pack; uncertain commit and conflicting duplicates|#4 #5 #17 #28; prerequisites #27 and applicable #26|
|3–4: recovery and artifacts|PE-02 A/B/A convergence; PE-03 claim/relationship evidence; PE-07 completion observations; worker ordering, missing endpoints and retention|#8 #9 #10 #14 #18 #19 #20 #29 #30|
|5: retrieval|Exact supporting events and excluded edges; uncertain negative answers; bounded pagination/deadlines|#6 #7 #24 #25 #31 #32|
|6: historical acceptance|Replay/rebuild/cutover, pack visibility and complete bounded Spanner journeys|#11 #12 #13 #21 #22|

PE identifiers refer to the persisted Astra report below. Existing issue associations are not evidence those issues already contain or implement the expanded scope. Track the disposition of each finding here and update affected implementation issues before executing each slice. Do not open eight duplicate bugs automatically.

### Acceptance checklist
- [ ] Resolve blocking contract decisions in slice1 and document the chosen policies; do not assume last-write-wins.
- [ ] Every one of23 PDLC event declarations has a contract and exact supported/no-op/extraction-only/refused classification; seven currently lack deterministic domain rules.
- [ ] Each event has fixture-linked normalized values, exact artifacts/evidence or deliberate no-op, invalid inputs and retrieval expectations.
- [ ] CRM and an unfamiliar compatible pack exercise the same mechanisms without adding engine type-name switches.
- [ ] Test omitted versus null fields, mismatched lists/write bounds, A/B/A and competing subscriber updates, same-ID changed content, revision mismatch, disabled required worker, duplicate/replay and partial failure.
- [ ] Separate real public records/documents, reconstructed webhook wrappers and synthetic cases; retain source gaps explicitly. Current captures have not been executed.
- [ ] Run applicable end-to-end journeys through actual Engram→Spanner, recording bounds, fingerprints, exact outcomes, defects and cleanup in the existing run ledger. No Redis/Neo4j runners or memory substitution for these cloud journeys.
- [ ] Independent review and targeted acceptance evidence support each completed slice; no blanket compatibility claim from source inspection or counts.

### Scope guardrails
Reuse current registry, adapters, projector, consumers, evaluation and tracking. Add only demonstrated missing checks/metadata. Automatic adapter generation through PRs, general raw-capture infrastructure and a new orchestration service are outside this feature's critical path. No Redis-to-Spanner migration. Future packs must stay within supported DSL/capabilities; arbitrary ontology formats/algorithms are not promised.

### Persisted design and evidence (current working tree, not yet committed)
- docs/review/2026-10-06-spanner-compatibility-plan.md
- docs/review/spanner-compatibility/2026-10-07-astra-pack-engine-design-review.md
- docs/review/spanner-compatibility/2026-10-07-astra-pack-engine-design-review-prompt.md
- docs/review/spanner-compatibility/pdlc-event-contract-inventory.csv
- docs/review/spanner-compatibility/pdlc-payload-experiment-matrix.csv
- docs/review/spanner-compatibility/public-payload-corpus/discovery-pass.md

Astra review was code/document/corpus inspection only; no new runtime tests or cloud calls. Existing defect and compatibility statuses remain unchanged.
title: Feature: reusable ontology-pack integration contracts and conformance

body:
## Reproduction
Baseline feature/engram-walkthrough 6a30dcf; all five Engram ports use actual Spanner, project portiq-mvp, instance engram-experiment, disposable engram DB. No runtime source changes or alternative backend.
Run scripts/engram_spanner_compat.py --phase retention-completion --disposable-engram-confirmed with explicit credential bootstrap. Six API-ingested/projected Events span fresh, warm, cold and archive ages. Warm Event has two low-score SIMILAR_TO edges and one high-score edge; Event nodes legitimately have no similarity_score property.
POST /v1/admin/prune for both warm and cold tiers, dry_run=true and false. All four return HTTP500 Internal server error. No API pruning occurs. Actual worker forgetting independently removes two low-score edges, preserves the high-score edge, and deletes one archive-age graph Event; all six ledger documents remain.

Evidence: docs/review/spanner-compatibility/runs/20261006-cloud-retention-completion-3dbff638/warm-prune-api.json and nonzero-archive-and-cold-prune.json. The earlier bce5e865 attempt preserves the Python TypeError stack; the corrected HTTP harness records responses separately from worker success.

## Cause
GraphOperationReads.events_for_pruning in src/context_graph/adapters/graph_ops.py supplies similarity_score=None from normal Event properties. domain.forgetting.should_prune_warm takes event_data.get("similarity_score",1.0), which returns None when present, then compares None < float. admin.prune calculates every tier's actions before selecting the requested tier, so cold requests also crash if a warm Event exists. Scores actually live on SIMILAR_TO relationships. Merely replacing None with1 would avoid the exception but could hide eligible relationship pruning.

## Acceptance criteria
Normalize absent values safely and derive warm candidates/counts from actual eligible relationships. Exercise warm and cold mixed-age fixtures, absent/null scores, multiple outgoing low-score edges and a retained high-score edge, dry-run no writes, live exact counts and cascading cleanup, plus truncated-scan reporting. Confirm API and scheduled worker apply consistent retention rules while retaining ledger history. Run against real Spanner, independently review counts and candidate semantics.

Shared pruning/graph-operations integration failure reproduced on Spanner; no cloud outage or service-specific fault injected. Priority high; estimate medium.
title: Make admin warm and cold pruning handle missing node similarity scores

body:
Branch feature/engram-walkthrough, baseline 6a30dcf. Real Engram API, actual projection consumer and all five Spanner storage ports against portiq-mvp/engram-experiment/engram. No Redis/Neo4j/memory substitution or runtime source edits.

## Reproduction and evidence
Evidence: docs/review/spanner-compatibility/runs/20261006-cloud-context-completion-6c14d9b2/context-query-budget.json. Set engine query timeout to 0.03s; wrap graph._query with a synthetic 0.12s delay then call the unchanged actual Spanner query. Context responds HTTP200 after 0.703s. No real service outage claimed; the controlled delay demonstrates the configured read budget is not enforced.

## Cause and impact
RetrievalEngine.get_context forwards timeout_s to graph read operations. GraphOperationReads.session_events_page and session_edges accept but ignore it. SpannerGraphStore._query uses snapshot.execute_sql without an SDK timeout, via asyncio.to_thread. Slow reads can exceed the configured read budget and tie up request work.

## Acceptance criteria
Define whether the setting bounds each graph operation or the complete request, then enforce that documented contract. Propagate remaining deadlines to native SDK reads as well as async waits; cancelling a to_thread await alone does not stop remote work. Return a deliberate timeout/partial-result response, preserve ordinary context behavior, and test delayed query/cancellation/shutdown with bounded fixtures. Review all graph read operations accepting timeout_s for the same gap.

Priority high. Estimate medium; native cancellation/deadline behavior requires review. This is shared deadline propagation plus Spanner SDK enforcement, not a measured production latency incident.
title: Enforce retrieval graph read budgets through Spanner SDK deadlines

body:
Branch feature/engram-walkthrough, baseline 6a30dcf. Real Engram API, actual projection consumer and all five Spanner storage ports against portiq-mvp/engram-experiment/engram. No Redis/Neo4j/memory substitution or runtime source edits.

## Reproduction and evidence
Run `context-completion` in scripts/engram_spanner_compat.py with the disposable guard. Evidence: docs/review/spanner-compatibility/runs/20261006-cloud-context-completion-6c14d9b2/context-distinct-pages.json.
Ingest and project five Events in one session with distinct occurrence seconds 0..4. GET /v1/context/{session}?max_nodes=2, then follow the returned cursor. First page returns events 4 and 3; second returns event 4 again, has_more=false. Events 0..2 are omitted. Five tied timestamps cover all five in the separate control.

## Cause and impact
GraphOperationReads.session_events_page in src/context_graph/adapters/graph_ops.py:1518 starts newest_first, then selects occurred_at greater than the cursor and sorts ascending. The continuation contradicts the initial ordering. Shared graph-operation bug reproduced on Spanner; context silently loses older evidence and double counts access on repeated nodes.

## Acceptance criteria
Use one deterministic timestamp plus event-ID ordering and matching continuation predicate across every page. Stable fixtures must cover every ID exactly once, tied and distinct timestamps, empty session, final short page, and access updates exactly once. Preserve node limits and compatible cursor semantics. Review cursor handling independently.

Priority high. Estimate small-to-medium; pagination migration compatibility needs review.
title: Keep context cursor ordering consistent across distinct event timestamps

body:
Priority: P1 (silent causal graph incompleteness). Estimate: 1–2 days. Layer: shared projection dependency handling with Spanner endpoint writes.

When a child referencing a valid parent event ID is accepted and projected before the parent exists, its CAUSED_BY edge is skipped and the delivery acknowledged. Later acceptance/projection of the parent does not repair that link.

Verified reproduction: `20261006-cloud-ordering-races-28efabf7`, `late_causal_parent_repairs_acknowledged_child_edge`. API ingress and actual projection loops use real Spanner; no synthetic storage failures or alternate backend.

1. Allocate the parent UUID, POST a child with parent_event_id pointing to it and drain projection.
2. POST the parent, then drain projection in a separate flush.
3. Both Event nodes exist, but child→parent CAUSED_BY is absent. The receipt includes before/after edges and exact event IDs. This is not a case where the parent never arrived.

Evidence: `docs/review/spanner-compatibility/runs/20261006-cloud-ordering-races-28efabf7/causal-parent-later.json`, observations and saved harness.

Code: domain projection computes the declared CAUSED_BY edge; `SpannerGraphStore._upsert_edges` writes only edges whose endpoints exist. Projection acknowledges the child without a durable unresolved dependency or later parent reconciliation. Existing #18 covers stale FOLLOWS cache between replicas, a separate order/link defect; #10 covers pack extraction evidence.

Acceptance criteria

- Preserve the declared causal dependency across separate flushes, worker restart and cross-session parent arrivals. Resolve it when the parent becomes available, without phantom complete lineage.
- Define bounded behavior when a parent never arrives; surface incompleteness rather than silently treating an omitted link as a complete causal history.
- Existing same-batch and parent-first cases remain correct and idempotent. Avoid changing per-session arrival-order FOLLOWS semantics.
- Exercise ingestion→actual projection→lineage API with before/after parent arrival on real Spanner.

Review expectations: independently assert ledger rows, both graph Events, exact CAUSED_BY identity and lineage evidence after resolution. No runtime fix performed.
title: Repair CAUSED_BY links when the accepted causal parent projects later

body:
Priority: P1 (silent loss of accepted asynchronous enrichment). Estimate: 1–2 days. Layer: shared worker/graph dependency handling, reproduced on real Spanner.

An actual EnrichmentConsumer can process and ACK an event before ProjectionConsumer creates its graph Event. Keywords and the computed384-dimensional vector are silently discarded, then later projection creates the Event with empty keywords and no vector. No delivery remains to repair the result.

Verified reproduction: run `20261006-cloud-ordering-races-28efabf7`, `enrichment_first_preserves_keywords_and_embedding_after_projection`. All storage ports use real Spanner, with only the embedding provider scripted.

1. POST observation.input with tool_name race-tool and importance_hint7.
2. Drain actual EnrichmentConsumer before starting projection. Its pending count reaches0.
3. Drain actual ProjectionConsumer.
4. The Event has importance7 from the original hint, keywords[] and no embedding; expected keywords observation/input/race-tool and384-vector were lost.

Evidence: `docs/review/spanner-compatibility/runs/20261006-cloud-ordering-races-28efabf7/enrichment-before-projection.json`, observations and saved harness.

Code: `worker/enrichment.py::process_message` treats update calls as success. `adapters/graph_ops.py::_update_existing` returns False when the Event is absent; `update_event_enrichment`/`store_event_embedding` discard that result. BaseConsumer acknowledges the successful return. Later projection has no enrichment repair path. The analogous pack extraction evidence race is #10; this issue is core keyword/vector enrichment loss, not a duplicate of that pack edge fix.

Acceptance criteria

- Missing graph Event must defer enrichment or persist enough work to reconcile after projection. Do not ACK away the sole pending enrichment before it can be applied.
- Verify actual independent worker ordering both ways, duplicate/restart deliveries, disabled/failing provider and graph storage failures.
- Once the Event exists, its intended keywords/importance/vector are applied without duplicate side effects; do not erase authoritative updates during repair.
- Bound retry/dependency handling and distinguish expected projection lag from permanent missing documents (#19) and the existing live retry gap (#14).

Review expectations: independent real Spanner API→enrichment-before-projection test, pending/ACK observations and final graph properties. No runtime fix performed.
title: Preserve enrichment when its worker runs before Event projection

body:
A Spanner transient write error becomes an unhandled HTTP500 on single-event ingestion, even after the adapter translates it to the neutral UnavailableError. The committed-prefix outcome path provides per-event errors, but failure in the first chunk escapes `_append_outcomes_sync` and `/v1/events` does not handle it deliberately.

Priority: P2. Estimate: 0.5–1 day including focused API fault/retry checks. Layer: shared ingestion API error contract, reproduced with Spanner; no claim of a real service outage.

Verified reproduction

Run `20261006-cloud-subscriptions-7700ac35`, subcheck `uncertain_commit_API_retry_duplicate_preserves_payload`. All storage ports are real Spanner against disposable `portiq-mvp/engram-experiment/engram`.

1. In test-only code wrap `SpannerEventLog._append_chunk_sync`: call the original to complete a real commit, then raise `google.api_core.exceptions.ServiceUnavailable` to simulate a lost commit response.
2. POST a valid new event to `/v1/events`.
3. The adapter translates the exception to `context_graph.ports.errors.UnavailableError`; the API returns500.
4. Remove the injection and retry the identical event. The API returns201 with status duplicate, the original position and preserved payload. Idempotence works; the failure is the first response/error contract.

Evidence: `docs/review/spanner-compatibility/runs/20261006-cloud-subscriptions-7700ac35/uncertain-commit-retry.json` and `execution.log`, plus the saved harness.

Relevant code: `src/context_graph/adapters/spanner/log.py::_append_outcomes_sync` raises on first-chunk failure; `adapters/spanner/errors.py::translate_spanner_error` maps ServiceUnavailable; `api/routes/events.py::ingest_event` only handles returned failed outcomes, and the generic API exception path responds500.

Acceptance criteria

- Define and implement explicit HTTP/retry semantics for neutral storage failures on single, batch and import ingress, including failure before commit and an uncertain commit response. Transient storage unavailability should return a deliberate retryable response rather than generic500.
- Preserve committed prefixes and per-event positions/errors. Do not claim that an uncertain request wrote nothing.
- Retry the same event IDs without duplicate ledger rows or changed original payloads.
- Verify first-chunk and later-chunk errors through Engram API boundaries and at least one real Spanner fault-injected journey; distinguish synthetic injection from a cloud outage.

Review expectations: independently check HTTP status/body, committed rows and safe retries; inspect for unintended changes to validation/refusal and streamed import behavior. No runtime fix has been made.
title: Handle first-chunk Spanner storage failures deliberately in ingestion APIs

body:
Valid application JSON collides with the Spanner float encoding marker. A literal singleton object {"$float":"0.125"} is accepted through Engram ingestion but reads back as the number0.125. The valid object {"$float":"ordinary-text"} is also accepted, then makes the stored document unreadable with ValueError while decoding.

Real-Spanner reproduction `20261006-cloud-json-22af9759`:
1. POST `/v1/events` with a valid observation event and payload.literal_object equal to either object above; HTTP201.
2. Read the event through Engram `EventLog.get_documents` on real Spanner.
3. Numeric marker changes object shape; text marker raises `could not convert string to float: ordinary-text`.
Exact receipts `numeric_tag.json` and `text_tag.json`, manifest/harness/API logs retained. The problem is specific to the Spanner JSON encoding/decoding path; no alternate backend runner was used.

Root cause in `src/context_graph/adapters/spanner/log.py`: `_encode_floats` emits {"$float":repr(value)} for floats but does not escape identical user objects; `_decode_float` treats any singleton object with that string key as its own number encoding. `json_value` runs that hook recursively for ledger documents and graph properties. An ordinary payload can corrupt shape or fail document loading, affecting projection/extraction/replay.

Acceptance criteria:
- Use an unambiguous codec/escaping strategy that distinguishes encoder-generated markers from arbitrary valid user JSON, including nested marker-shaped objects and nonnumeric strings.
- Preserve the existing exact-float workaround required by real Spanner, normal lists/null/bools/unicode and finite float values.
- Decide and document backward-read/migration behavior for already-stored ambiguous cells; do not silently lose original objects or make a codec upgrade unreplayable.
- Verify API ingest→real Spanner ledger read→worker projection, as well as graph-property round trips; bad internal encoding should raise a translated/clear storage error rather than silently change application data.

Priority P1 (accepted content is changed or becomes unreadable); medium estimate. Independent review should assess codec versioning, legacy data and mixed payloads. No runtime fix included in this audit.
title: Escape literal JSON objects that collide with Spanner float markers

body:
Engram API shutdown does not release the Spanner database session manager. The all-Spanner store bundle registers zero close callbacks; the SDK session and its renewal thread remain alive after API lifespan exits.

Verified on real Spanner by `20261006-cloud-shutdown-71530641`, exact receipt `SDK-shutdown.json`: all five backends=spanner, registered_closers0, database_close_calls_after_app_shutdown0, SDK_session_retained=true, SDK_background_thread_alive=true. The normal API health endpoint returned200 before shutdown. The harness then explicitly closed only its owned SDK database; `SDK-manual-cleanup.json` retained. No data/schema changes.

Test-only cleanup adjustment: the SDK's local session-renewal polling interval was reduced from its installed default600s to0.2s before this app's database was created, to bound manual cleanup. It does not change store-close registration or cloud operations; the missing runtime callback and retained session remain observable. Earlier `20261006-cloud-shutdown-9df04375` used a nonexistent health/detailed route and then blocked in default SDK cleanup; that attempt was terminated and recorded as a harness failure, not this product reproduction. Its remote session deletion is unverified rather than hidden.

Root cause in `src/context_graph/adapters/registry.py`: `open_stores` creates/uses the Spanner Database but never registers its close lifecycle in `_closers`. `Stores.close` promises to release held connections and simply invokes that list. Redis/Neo4j/GCS paths register cleanup, whereas Spanner does not. No other backend runner was launched for this test.

Acceptance criteria:
- Register exactly one owned Spanner database/session-manager cleanup for a store bundle sharing it across log/graph/search/subscriptions.
- API shutdown and worker shutdown invoke it, including failed startup/partial construction; make repeated cleanup safe.
- Avoid blocking the event loop or hanging shutdown on SDK renewal polling; retain an explicit bounded shutdown strategy compatible with the installed driver.
- Verify real session/background-task termination, not merely that Stores.close returns; preserve externally owned databases/schema/data.

Priority P2; medium estimate. Independent review should inspect ownership across all five ports, construction failures and real SDK shutdown behavior. No runtime fix included in this audit.
title: Release owned Spanner SDK session managers on API and worker shutdown

body:
Real Spanner native ANN returns matching Entity IDs, but the agent-memory subgraph engine can discard every vector seed and return no nodes even when those entities have real Event reference evidence in the requested session. A healthy graph seed channel masks this gap.

Verified cloud run `20261006-cloud-vector-9f8fc3ca`, exact receipt `vector-only-existing-session.json`.
Fixture setup from `20261006-cloud-endpoints-fa84c6f7`: seven API-ingested/projected Events in tied-context; four384-dimensional Entity vectors via the public graph write port; actual Event REFERENCES Entity links to the self/near matches. Native forced-index ANN top-k2 correctly returns self then near; threshold0.99 returns only self.

Isolation reproduction:
- Request `/v1/query/subgraph` for the existing tied-context session.
- Use a fixed384-dimensional query vector, disable keyword retrieval, and control the graph seed orchestration stage to return no seeds. Storage ports remain real Spanner; this is explicit channel isolation, not a claimed Cloud Spanner outage.
- Response meta reports vector3 and seed_nodes includes entity:compat-self, entity:compat-near and entity:compat-orthogonal, but nodes={} and edges=[]. Diagnostic persisted edges include same-session Event REFERENCES Entity evidence.
An additional naturally empty graph-session request also produced the empty result, but the same-session controlled test removes session-filter ambiguity.

Root cause: `RetrievalEngine._fetch_seed_nodes` fetches only Event properties, appends unfetched Entity IDs to seed_node_ids, then `_expand_neighbors` calls the Event-only/outgoing `GraphReads.event_neighbors` contract. Shared graph reads key those seeds as (Event,id). There is no hydration or inbound Event-reference expansion for Entity vector seeds. This is a shared orchestration/graph-read mismatch confirmed on real Spanner, not proven Spanner-exclusive.

Acceptance criteria:
- Vector Entity seeds yield useful returned Entity/evidence context through a typed read contract, including the associated Event REFERENCES relationships.
- Preserve explicit session/admission filtering and provenance, rather than accidentally using a global unrestricted expansion.
- Validate vector-only, graph-only, keyword-only and combined retrieval, including empty other channels and channel failures; retain native ANN score/rank/top-k/threshold semantics.
- Through the Engram HTTP API, this fixture must return the intended Entity/evidence nodes when graph seeds are empty, not silently report successful empty context despite positive native matches.

Priority P2; medium estimate. Independent review should check label/key handling, edge direction, session scope and degradation semantics. No runtime fix included in this audit.
title: Hydrate Entity vector seeds and retrieve their event reference evidence

body:
The real Engram lineage HTTP API violates its advertised node capacity and stops pagination before covering a known causal chain.

Reproduction on real Spanner:
1. Ingest seven events in one session through `/v1/events/batch`, each event after the first having the preceding event as parent; run the actual projection loop.
2. Request the last event's `/v1/nodes/{id}/lineage?max_depth=10&max_nodes=3`: returns4 unique nodes while meta.capacity says max_nodes3, used_nodes4.
3. Paginate the same chain with max_nodes2: first page contains3 nodes and cursor Mg==; second contains4 nodes then has_more=false. The union covers only4 of7 events.

Verified twice: `20261006-cloud-endpoints-f098c7f4` (bound), `20261006-cloud-endpoints-fa84c6f7` (bound and pagination). Exact receipts `bounded-lineage.json` and `lineage-pages.json` under the latter run; API requests/worker/input harness retained. Tied-occurrence context pagination on the same fixture correctly covers all7 events, isolating the lineage path.

Root cause in `RetrievalEngine.get_lineage` (`src/context_graph/retrieval/engine.py`): max_nodes caps the number of path records, then merges every node from those paths without enforcing a unique-node cap. Every page refetches only clamped_nodes+1 path records and slices that prefix by offset, so later paths are never fetched. Spanner's TRAIL query also needs a stable paging order rather than unordered LIMIT-based path prefixes. The engine-level defects are shared; the failure was confirmed on Spanner rather than asserted exclusive to it.

Acceptance criteria:
- Bound unique returned nodes by max_nodes; include only edges whose endpoints are represented, with truthful truncation/capacity.
- Advance pages beyond the first fetched prefix, with stable cursor/order semantics for branching and cyclic graphs; do not end while eligible ancestors remain.
- Verify all7 nodes are reachable across pages of this fixture and each page respects its cap; missing-node, depth and upper limits continue to work.
- Recheck through Engram HTTP endpoints against real Spanner, including branching/cyclic paths and graph mutation between pages.

Priority P2; medium estimate. Independent review should examine both the shared engine pagination contract and native GQL path ordering. No runtime fix included in this audit.
title: Bound lineage nodes and advance pagination beyond the first path prefix

body:
Engram API startup succeeds and serves healthy when `CG_SPANNER_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS=3` against the existing real Spanner GraphNodes embedding column fixed at 384. The first native vector search then raises `InvalidRequestError: APPROX_COSINE_DISTANCE: Array length mismatch: 3 and 384`.

Verified through a separate ordinary Engram API process using the test token bootstrap, followed by the real public vector-index port. No writes, database creation or schema changes occurred. Exact run: `20261006-cloud-schema-fd247214`; receipt: `docs/review/spanner-compatibility/runs/20261006-cloud-schema-fd247214/dimension_mismatch-startup.json`. DDL receipt contains `embedding ARRAY<FLOAT64>(vector_length=>384)`; configured dimensions are 3; served_health is true.

Reproduction:
1. Use the canonical existing Engram Spanner database with its 384-dimensional column/index, all five storage ports selecting Spanner, schema checking enabled and database creation disabled.
2. Set `CG_SPANNER_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS=3` and start the Engram API: health returns200.
3. Open the same Engram stores/settings and call `vector_index.nearest([1.0,0.0,0.0], top_k=1)`: native ANN request fails with the physical length mismatch.

Root cause: `schema_differences` in `src/context_graph/adapters/spanner/schema.py` compares table/column/index/graph names, not the configured vector length or physical column/index definition. `open_database` accepts this as compatible. `SpannerGraphStore` then uses the requested length to select its native ANN branch.

Acceptance criteria:
- Detect incompatible fixed vector dimensions during schema handshake and fail startup with a clear configured-vs-stored explanation; do not silently alter a user database or fallback to another backend.
- Check other schema type/index differences that affect runtime compatibility rather than considering matching names sufficient.
- Keep valid 384-dimensional database startup/search working, allow harmless extra schema elements, and respect database creation guards.
- Reproduce the mismatch using actual Engram API startup plus native Spanner search; verify the translated error and no schema/data mutations.

Priority P2; medium estimate. Independent review should check metadata discovery permissions, older schemas/index definitions and refusal behavior. No runtime fix included in this compatibility audit.
title: Reject incompatible Spanner vector dimensions during schema handshake

body:
On the real Spanner compatibility target, a successfully rebuilt/evaluated PDLC graph is reported by `/v1/admin/stats` as containing only 9 Event nodes and 6 FOLLOWS edges. The database contains 19 registered domain nodes plus one OntologyState record, and 25 edges. WorkItem, Change, Review, TestRun, Release, Deployment and all PDLC relationship counts are omitted.

Reproduction (existing disposable real-Spanner target):
1. Enable all five Spanner storage ports and the PDLC pack.
2. Ingest the eight signed GitHub/Jira fixture deliveries plus its extraction observation, project, and rebuild into the second database; the 11-question evaluation passes at F1=1.0.
3. Read `/v1/admin/stats` against that target.
4. Compare with diagnostic `SELECT label, COUNT(*) FROM GraphNodes GROUP BY label` and equivalent GraphEdges aggregation.

Verified run: `20261006-cloud-stats-a4a0c509`; exact HTTP/SQL receipt: `docs/review/spanner-compatibility/runs/20261006-cloud-stats-a4a0c509/pack-stats.json`. The assertion fails with `admin stats omit or miscount ontology labelWorkItem`. Earlier attempt `20261006-cloud-stats-67dad977` had a harness KeyError using a nested response shape; retain it as a harness mistake, not independent reproduction.

Root cause: `GraphOps.get_graph_stats` in `src/context_graph/adapters/graph_ops.py` enumerates fixed STATS_NODE_LABELS and STATS_EDGE_TYPES and sums those subsets. This is a shared graph-contract defect exposed on Spanner, not proven exclusive to Spanner. Runtime/rebuild code also consumes these stats; pack-only graphs must not be treated as empty because their types are absent from the list.

Acceptance criteria:
- Stats include active pack node/relationship types with truthful totals; document explicitly whether ontology control records are included.
- Core/memory and PDLC/CRM/custom pack counts work without adding each pack to a static core list.
- Counts remain complete beyond read-page limits; use a suitable backend aggregation/count contract rather than counting capped discovery results.
- Validate through the real Engram admin endpoint against populated and empty Spanner graphs; check callers using total_nodes for rebuild safety.

Priority: P2 (misleading operational reporting, potentially unsafe graph-emptiness guards). Estimate: medium, shared counting contract plus backend implementation and endpoint verification. Independent review should verify pack coverage, pagination and rebuild callers. No runtime fix included in this audit.

Admin replay cannot advance through a ledger with at least100 events sharing an occurrence timestamp on Spanner. Its cursor is only the last occurrence time; the Spanner event search applies an inclusive `>=` boundary. The next page therefore returns the same100 events.

Confirmed through actual Engram batch ingestion of128 events to real Spanner. Reading the two pages with the exact EventQuery used by admin replay produces identical ID lists. A separate real API process exercises `/v1/admin/replay`, with a hard request/process deadline so no runaway replay is left behind.

Evidence: `docs/review/spanner-compatibility/runs/20261006-cloud-replay-93151f94/` contains the exact runner, `replay-pages.json`, API log, observations and owned-process cleanup receipt. Reproduce on a disposable deployment with all ports on Spanner: `PYTHONPATH=src:. python scripts/engram_spanner_compat.py --phase replay --disposable-engram-confirmed`.

Cause: `api/routes/admin.py` pages by `prev_event.occurred_at`; `adapters/spanner/log.py` uses `occurred_at_ms >= after_ms`. Timestamp-only pagination cannot distinguish ties. Repeated pages make progress impossible and may starve other events indefinitely after clearing the graph.

Acceptance criteria:
- Replay uses a stable complete cursor (prefer the ledger replay/log-position abstraction), advancing across timestamp ties and interleaved sessions.
-128/100/101 tied events finish with each unique event projected exactly once and no missing events.
- Preserve session-correct lineage and pack-driven projection/evaluation state; review those semantics separately rather than only replacing >= with >, which drops tied events.
- Bound replay/no-progress behavior and report incomplete work honestly on failures.
- Regression exercises real Engram replay over a Spanner ledger, with a process deadline.

Scope: medium replay traversal change; review paging and projection semantics. This is same-backend replay, not Redis-to-Spanner migration.
title: Make Spanner admin replay advance across tied event timestamps

## Problem

The completeness plugin treats links not returned by bounded reads as absent. `truncated=true` is set, but individual nodes are still labeled `no_link`, and completeness counters still report absence. An unchecked relationship is not proof of a missing relationship.

## Verified reproduction

Project the existing 11-event CRM fixture into memory. Acme has deals. Run:
`ArtifactQuery(query="Which accounts have no deals?", seed_node_ids=("Account:acme",), intent="coverage")`.
With normal budgets, Acme is not reported. With `ArtifactRetriever(max_graph_calls=1, ...)`, observed: `Account:acme` has `retrieval_reason=no_link`, while `meta.truncated=true`. Its links were never checked.

Evidence: `retrieval/artifacts.py:315` (`_spend`), `:324` (`_neighbors_all`), `:815` (`_missing_links`), especially `status.get(..., "no_link")`. The same risk applies when a subject's edge range is truncated, not just call-budget exhaustion.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Track whether each subject's relationship check completed. Distinguish confirmed absence from unknown/incomplete evidence.
- [ ] Do not label an unchecked/partially checked subject `no_link`, or count it as a proven missing link. Select and document a compatible response/error behavior.
- [ ] Return clear partial-result metadata identifying what could not be checked.
- [ ] Add memory regressions for budget exhaustion, a single node/edge-type range exceeding neighbor limits, and an unseen confirmed edge after returned proposed/rejected edges.
- [ ] Preserve correct results for genuinely missing links and the existing CRM/PDLC evaluation sets.

Priority: high for trustworthy answers. Estimate: M. Preserve budgets; fix the inference rather than simply raising limits or introducing a new retrieval engine.

## Review basis and closure

Verified at commit `6a30dcfd376d21b2732ffc36b8ed8847abb2a9de`. Existing focused pack/ingest/retrieval tests: **95 passed, 2 integration cases deselected**. These probes expose missing regressions; they are not fixed yet. Deliver a focused PR linking this issue with acceptance-test evidence and an independent review before closure.
title: Do not report missing artifact links when completeness reads are incomplete

body:
## Problem

Ordinary API clients can grant themselves the trust of an allowlisted importer by supplying its agent ID. The API blocks `webhook:` IDs, but permits other trusted IDs; `PackProjector` derives trust solely from membership in the configured source allowlist. This affects admission and corroboration in the new artifact engine.

## Verified reproduction

On the memory backend with CRM active, configure `CG_ONTOLOGY_TRUSTED_SOURCES=importer:crm` and an ordinary API key. Post `crm.account.created` using that ordinary key with `agent_id=importer:crm`. Observed: HTTP 201, then the planned Account has `source_trust=trusted`. There is no credential-to-importer binding.

Evidence: `api/routes/events.py:92`, `api/dependencies.py:98`, `domain/pack_projection.py:300`, `settings.py:570`. The reserved webhook-ID guard works; this finding concerns non-webhook trusted identities.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Define a credential-bound trusted-source contract for generic ingest and privileged imports. A caller-supplied agent ID alone cannot grant source trust.
- [ ] Apply the contract consistently to single, batch and NDJSON import paths; preserve the existing signed-webhook trust boundary.
- [ ] Prove an ordinary API-key holder cannot impersonate another trusted importer. Prove authorized imports and signed GitHub/Jira events still project trusted provenance.
- [ ] Document local development behavior, shared deployment requirements and compatibility for already stored events. Do not silently relabel historical ledger documents.
- [ ] Add adversarial memory API-to-projection-to-retrieval tests; ensure admission cannot be bypassed by the spoofed identity.

Priority: high for shared access. Estimate: M. Coordinate with payload validation #4, but keep identity/auth validation distinct from payload shape. Reuse current auth/provenance machinery; a general identity platform is not required.

## Review basis and closure

Verified at commit `6a30dcfd376d21b2732ffc36b8ed8847abb2a9de`. Existing focused pack/ingest/retrieval tests: **95 passed, 2 integration cases deselected**. These probes expose missing regressions; they are not fixed yet. Deliver a focused PR linking this issue with acceptance-test evidence and an independent review before closure.
title: Bind pack source trust to authenticated ingress identity, not caller-supplied agent_id

body:
## Problem and evidence

Ingestion validates the shared event envelope and active-pack event namespace, but domain payloads are not validated against an event contract before ledger append. A declared event can therefore be accepted with missing or incorrectly typed projection inputs, leading to omitted nodes/properties or projection failure later.

Verified on `feature/engram-walkthrough` at `6a30dcf`:
- `src/context_graph/domain/ontology.py:300`: `EventDef` contains aliases and a note, but no payload schema.
- `src/context_graph/api/ingest.py:87`: `check_events` validates `Event` and envelope invariants; payloads remain dictionaries.
- `src/context_graph/api/routes/events.py:92`: ontology admission checks event type, not domain payload fields.
- `src/context_graph/api/routes/webhooks.py:173`: translated payloads are appended without a shared payload-validation step.

## Intended behavior

Keep one common event envelope. Each ontology pack declares an event-specific payload contract. A shared validator checks normalized events after source translation and before ledger writes. For example, a CRM deal-created event missing a required string deal ID must receive a field-level rejection instead of silently failing to create a Deal.

Use the existing pack model, registry and ingest helpers. This does not require a separate ingestion pipeline or Python adapter for each ontology.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Extend pack event declarations with an explicit, bounded payload contract: required fields, supported types, optional fields and a documented extra-field/coercion policy. Reject invalid schema declarations at pack load.
- [ ] Add one shared validator resolving the contract by active event type. Errors identify event/index, payload field, and expected constraint without exposing the full payload.
- [ ] Enforce it on single ingest, batch ingest, NDJSON import and translated GitHub/Jira webhooks before the rejected event is appended. Single invalid input returns 422; batch/import preserve documented partial-acceptance and per-event outcomes. Specify webhook behavior for a delivery translating to multiple events, avoiding accidental partial writes.
- [ ] Declare contracts for current PDLC and CRM events from their actual producer/rule inputs; do not infer required payload fields from every node property. Decide and document compatibility for schema-less core/agent events, existing clients and historical replay.
- [ ] Preserve namespace ownership, signature/trust checks, deterministic IDs and dedup behavior. Historical replay must not silently rewrite the ledger.
- [ ] Prove valid CRM and PDLC payloads ingest, project and answer queries on the memory backend. Prove missing/wrong-type inputs do not enter the ledger across all ingest paths; keep existing fixtures passing.
- [ ] Update ADR-0018 and pack-authoring/bulk-import documentation with the selected contract and client migration behavior.

## Delivery and review

Priority: first. Estimate: M. Implement in a focused PR linking this issue; include before/after examples, acceptance-test results and compatibility decisions. Close only after review and the end-to-end criteria pass. Do not add a new schema service, queue or adapter framework without a demonstrated need.

## Reproduction added during the focused review

With CRM loaded and all storage ports on memory, post `crm.deal.created` with payload `{"title":"Missing ID"}` and a valid envelope. Observed: **HTTP 201**, **one ledger event**, and **zero planned Deal nodes**. The required identity is missing, but the event is accepted and cannot project its intended artifact.

The focused existing pack/ingest/retrieval suite passes (**95 passed, 2 integration cases deselected**); this missing-key scenario needs a new regression. Review the accompanying trust, completeness, rejected-link, lookup and provenance issues together when drafting the implementation plan.
title: Validate pack-specific event payloads before ledger append
